why: ADR-090 §6 ordered this artifact and nobody built it (checked 2026-09-08:
`data/chunk-policy-registry.json` did not exist). Two separate needs land on
the same table, so it is one table:
(a) STATUS. A policy artifact's sha256 IS its identity -- it is pinned by
`build_config.json`, by every MANIFEST and by the shipped chunk@3 corpus,
and `chunk_policy.load_chunk_policy` validates an EXACT key set. So a
`status` field cannot be added to the artifact itself: it would change the
hash AND make the file unloadable. ADR-090 §6's mechanism is a sidecar
consulted at SELECTION time only; the artifacts stay byte-identical and
readable forever (I2 rule 2; ADR-039).
(b) FAMILY. `specs/epochs.md` §5 says that if a third chunker family appears,
'split the family formally (chunk.generic, chunk.law) rather than widening
the scope again'. ADR-090 §3 made that split, and ADR-090 §4 scoped
'standardize on 1152' to `chunk.generic` alone. But the family a policy
belongs to was never written down anywhere a program can read: task 535
measured a 3.73x median granularity change across 82 hosts and NOTHING in
the repo could see it, because 84 of 86 sealed families declare
`chunk_policy.policy_id: "unknown"` and no artifact states which family a
policy serves. This table is where that lives.
READ AT SELECTION TIME, NEVER AT REPLAY TIME. A historical reproduction loads
the artifact by sha256 and ignores this file entirely (`--replay`); that is the
whole point of a sidecar. A NEW materialization that selects a `superseded`
policy is refused.
ratified_by: Tim's merge of PR #108 (task 541, the mechanism) and PR #130 (ADR-090 amendment 1, the ruling), 2026-09-09
consulted_by: cytir/chunk/reference_selector.py (which family a page belongs to)
cytir/sources/contract.py (a family may not declare a superseded policy)

chunk.generic.what: The structured markdown packer for generic prose and documentation. ADR-079 scoped it; ADR-090 §3 named it.

chunk.law.what: Per-article splitters over source-native anchors (fedlex Akoma Ntoso, ch_cantonal_law, ch_zh_fulltext, de_laender_*). ADR-090 §3/§4: out of scope for the generic policy, own counter, and 'standardize on 1152' may NEVER be read as authority to sweep it in. Enforced today by the canonical materializer's `validate_page` (deny_source_types + non-empty-anchor refusal), which this registry restates rather than re-implements.

chunk.news.what: The daily news lane. ADR-090 §5: news keeps `legacy-180w-o30@1`, the one measured exception, on a 21,569-article / 6,000-query bake-off in which epoch 4 lost on every leg and every query shape.

chunk.reference.what: RATIFIED, ADR-090 amendment 1 (PR #130, option 2). Production-granularity boundaries for the pages the epoch-4 packer cut wider than the collection production serves -- the whole density class task 535 measured at a 3.73x median chunk-count drop and task 540 priced at 3,663,458 rows, SHORT PAGES INCLUDED. Selected per PAGE by chunk_reference_selector.py under data/chunk-reference-selector.v2.json, never per host. Epoch-4 width stays where ADR-090 measured it to win (Wikipedia) or to be a no-op (the single-unit families).

chunk.atomic.what: One source record, one chunk: sources whose own record boundary IS the passage boundary (registry rows, catalogue entries).

chunk.preserved.what: Not a chunker. Records the fact that a stage shard's text was RECOVERED from the retained store, never produced -- so it cannot be read as having been chunked under whichever policy happened to be current (task 505).

chunk.law.sub.what: PROPOSED, task 573 / E573-1 -- NOT ratified. Sub-chunks the BODY of a `chunk.law` article that is wider than the 288-word tail, at the widths `chunk.reference` already uses, and leaves shorter articles byte-identical. The article's source-native anchor and its `article_id`/`law_id` travel on every sub-chunk, so the outer per-article boundary ADR-090 4 protects is kept in both directions: `chunk.law` is not swept into the generic policy, and a long article stops being one wide vector. Ratification is ADR-090 amendment 2 and is Tim's merge; until then its policy is `proposed`, selectable only by an experiment arm (EXPERIMENT_SELECTABLE).

3f3e24823cf2e0851b149690b6c43d579e3b7d10.why: Task 631's ERIC-scoped measurement arm, minted per Tim's standing directive (2026-09-10, memory `tim-prefer-larger-chunks-fundamentals`): 'all else being equal we prefer larger chunks as that means a smaller index'. ERIC official-PDF is `chunk.generic` (generic prose/PDF, currently epoch 4 at 768w/1152-tail, measured at 40.6 chunks/doc on the 080000 sample -- the highest ratio of any measured family, `specs/portfolio-100m.md` fork F7b) and had never had a wider arm measured for it. Task 569 already minted a numerically-identical shape (soft_target 1024, hard_max 1536 = the ratified 1.5x guard, token_hard_max 2560 unchanged) for `chunk.reference` (epoch 7, `struct-md-1024w-o0-adjacent-sections-tail-1536-tok2560`) -- but that arm is explicitly scoped to Wikipedia-class short reference pages (task 569's own `why`) and was never recommended for `chunk.generic`. Rather than reuse the chunk.reference sha256/policy_id (which would conflate two families' measurement history under one identity and violate `chunk_policy_registry`'s per-family selection contract), this is a SEPARATE artifact: same generator (`struct-markdown-adjacent-section-pack-v1`), same overlap/merge/floor/tail/section_packing sub-blocks copied unchanged from the epoch-4 `chunk.generic` policy, only sizing.soft_target/word_guard.hard_max/prefix.maximum changed (1024/1536/128, same derivation rule task 569 used: hard_max = soft_target*1.5, prefix.maximum = soft_target//8). The policy_id carries an explicit `-generic-arm` suffix (deliberately NOT the bare `struct-md-1024w-o0-adjacent-sections-tail-1536-tok2560` name chunk.reference epoch 7 already owns) so the two families' identically-shaped-but-differently-scoped arms can never be confused by name, even though their sha256 already differs (the `policy_id` field is embedded in the file bytes, so a distinct string was required to get a distinct hash, not merely sufficient). `proposed`, selectable only via `assert_selectable(experiment=True)` -- this arm writes to no serving or candidate collection; it measures `chunk.generic` chunks/doc on one already-Docling'd ERIC tranche (010000) only, per the task631 brief.
3f3e24823cf2e0851b149690b6c43d579e3b7d10.admitted_for_families_why: ADR-113 (Tim, 2026-09-25): ratified selectable for `eric_official_pdf`'s own real extraction ONLY (`chunk_policy_registry.assert_selectable(..., family_id='eric_official_pdf')`), via the demand-reserve admission ruling (POLICY.md@v3.1 §5, fork F7b). Status stays `proposed`, not `current`: E631-1 cashed all three pre-registered STRUCTURAL predictions (30.06 chunks/doc, 0/7,515 over the 2,560-token ceiling, full 250-doc coverage), which is evidence enough for a bounded points ceiling, but says nothing about retrieval quality -- task 569's own W1024 arm lost ground on one held-out leg despite being structurally smaller. Promoting this arm to the shared `chunk.generic` default for every other family needs a held-out eval this ADR does not run.

epoch_counter.rule: specs/epochs.md §4 rule 2 -- epoch ints are monotonic per family, never reused, never decremented.
epoch_counter.decision: The split families chunk.generic / chunk.law / chunk.news / chunk.reference SHARE the one monotonic `chunk` counter rather than each starting a private one at 1. `rule_epochs.chunk` therefore stays a single comparable integer, which is what every existing generation discriminator relies on -- task 536 index_partition_hosts.py's --min-chunk-epoch/--max-chunk-epoch classifies a stage partition by exactly this int, and a private per-family counter would have made a chunk.reference row read as epoch 1. The FAMILY is read from `chunk_rule`/`policy_id` through this registry, never from the int.
epoch_counter.note_on_vocabulary: `policy_family` here (chunk.generic / chunk.law / chunk.news / chunk.reference / chunk.atomic / chunk.preserved) is ADR-090 §3's POLICY taxonomy: which boundary rule set a page is cut under. It is NOT chunk_provenance.FAMILIES (generic-structured / generic-legacy-window / law-article-117 / ...), which names the PRODUCER: which code emitted the row. The two axes are orthogonal and both are needed -- a chunk.reference row is produced by `generic-structured`, exactly like a chunk.generic row, because it is the same module under a different pinned artifact. Neither vocabulary may absorb the other (engineering-doctrine 1: a merged vocabulary would make 'which rule cut this row' unanswerable again).

why: ADR-090 amendment 1 widened `chunk.reference` from long, densely-
sectioned reference pages to the whole density class. That change is a
change of RULE, and a rule with no status is exactly what let a 3.73x
granularity change sweep 82 hosts unseen. So the selector artifacts get
the same treatment the policy artifacts got: identity is the sha256,
status lives in this sidecar, and `assert_selector_selectable` refuses a
superseded selector for a NEW materialization while replay still
reproduces the rows any historical selector produced.
